adjudication_records.issue_text: Google updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is dead code: when externalCalendarId is falsy, find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) always returns undefined, so legacy bookings without externalCalendarId target calendarId: undefined and can't be updated/deleted on destination calendar; delete path also lost the "primary" fallback

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the target calendar with:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

(and similarly for `calendarId` in `deleteEvent`). When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`null`/`undefined`), the `.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares `externalId` to `null/undefined` and will almost always return `undefined`, making this fallback effectively dead code. Prior code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly as the fallback.

This means legacy references lacking `externalCalendarId` will not select any destination calendar id from `event.destinationCalendar` and may call Google APIs with `calendarId: undefined` (or at least fail to target the intended destination calendar). The diff also shows `deleteEvent` now derives `calendarId` the same way, so the same issue applies there; whether it still falls back to `primary` at the API call site is not shown in the diff, but the destination-calendar fallback is clearly broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale `credential` variable in EventManager.update loop: credential is declared outside the reference loop and not reassigned when DB lookup fails, so updateEvent is called with the previous iteration's credential against the wrong calendar account

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `EventManager.update` logic, `credential` is reassigned at the start of each `reference.credentialId` iteration via `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0];` (so it becomes `undefined` if not found, not “stale” from a prior iteration). If the DB lookup also fails, `credential` remains `undefined`, but that is not reuse of a previous credential. Also, the `else` branch uses `for (const credential of credentials)` which *shadows* the outer `credential` variable rather than reusing it. Therefore the specific claim that `updateEvent` can be called with the previous iteration’s credential due to staleness is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google Meet fallback crashes on empty destinationCalendar array: destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined for [], then mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws TypeError; needs optional chaining
matched_golden_ids: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root bug: when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring yields an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar, and accessing properties on it (e.g., integration) causes a TypeError/null reference in createEvent/updateEvent. The candidate focuses on the empty-array case but matches the underlying failure mode the golden comment highlights.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Collective events: team members' destination calendars are dropped when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar, since evt.destinationCalendar is null and the push is skipped

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`... : null,` around the `evt` construction). Later, for collective team events, team members' destination calendars are appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional chain skips the push, dropping `teamDestinationCalendars` even if collected from team members earlier. This matches the finding and is a real behavioral defect introduced/exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule drops the user.destinationCalendar fallback entirely; bookings without booking-level destination calendar now get [] in reschedule flows

adjudication.rationale: In `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, the pre-change code set `destinationCalendar` to `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar`, which never referenced `user.destinationCalendar` as a fallback. The diff changes this to an array form (`bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [..] : []`), but it does not “drop” a `user.destinationCalendar` fallback because none existed in the shown code. (It is true the new code yields `[]` when no booking-level destination calendar exists, but the specific claim about removing a user fallback is not supported by the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: createEvent can report success/reference for events never created: CalendarManager.createEvent always includes externalId and credentialId even on failure, and EventManager persists a booking reference pointing at a nonexistent calendar event

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, `createEvent(...)` returns an `EventResult` object even when the underlying provider call fails (the catch returns `undefined` for `creationResult`, sets `success = false`, but the function still returns an object). The returned object now *always* includes `externalId` (passed in) and `credentialId` (`credential.id`) (see added fields in the return object). In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, code that builds/persists booking references uses `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` and `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` without checking `result.success` / `result.createdEvent` before producing a reference. This can create a calendar reference containing `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId` even when no calendar event was created (i.e., `createdEvent` is `undefined`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shared-reference mutation: evt.destinationCalendar wraps the same Prisma objects and push mutates in place, so repeated booking attempts in the same request scope accumulate duplicated destination calendars and create the event multiple times

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `evt.destinationCalendar` is constructed as a fresh array literal (e.g. `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : ...`) in `handleNewBooking.ts`, so `push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` only mutates that local array, not a shared array coming from Prisma. Wrapping Prisma objects in an array does not create a shared mutable array reference, and nothing in the diff shows “repeated booking attempts in the same request scope” reusing the same `evt` object such that destination calendars would accumulate across attempts. While duplicates could theoretically occur if `teamDestinationCalendars` itself contains duplicates, the specific claim of shared-reference accumulation causing multiple creates is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar interface change is only half-applied: createEvent's credentialId param is only used by Google; positional untyped arg risks silent fallback to "primary" creating events on the wrong calendar
loadUsers error handling swallows the real cause: try/catch converts all non-Prisma errors into generic 500 and Prisma errors into 400, masking the actual failure messages

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` was changed from a straight prisma call / mapping to a `try/catch` that rethrows `HttpError` or `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` as a new `HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`, and converts all other thrown errors into `HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. This does mask the original error details/stack for non-Prisma errors (and normalizes Prisma errors into 400), which can make diagnosing failures harder. This is a real, diff-grounded review concern, but it’s primarily about error transparency/observability rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager DB credential fetch has no ownership scoping (potential IDOR): prisma.credential.findUnique in EventManager.ts and handleCancelBooking.ts looks up credential purely by ID with no userId/teamId/organization constraint, loading foreign credentials' secret keys and using them to create/update/delete calendar events; should use findFirst({ where: { id, userId: organizer.id } })

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple DB fallbacks that load credentials by ID without any ownership/tenancy constraint. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, both `createAllCalendarEvents` and the calendar-update loop now call `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } ... })` / `where: { id: reference.credentialId }` with no `userId`/`teamId`/org scoping before using the returned `key`/auth data. Similarly, `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` adds `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` when the credential isn't found on the booking user. This matches the finding: it is a verifiable security defect introduced by the diff because it enables fetching arbitrary credential records by ID if an attacker can influence/poison the stored `credentialId` in destinationCalendar/references, and it also breaks the assumption that only the current user's credentials are used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google updateEvent/deleteEvent destination-calendar resolution in CalendarService.ts is dead code: in the else branch externalCalendarId is falsy so find(... === externalCalendarId) never matches and calendarId ends up undefined, causing updates/deletes to hit the wrong or default/primary calendar; should resolve against event.destinationCalendar by credentialId or fall back to primary explicitly

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendar id as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), the `.find(... === externalCalendarId)` compares against `undefined`/`null`, so it will not match a real `externalId` and returns `undefined`. This makes the destination-calendar resolution effectively dead/wrong in that branch and can cause updates/deletes to fall back to an unintended calendar (or pass an undefined calendarId depending on later defaults). This defect is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: credential may be undefined when passed to updateEvent in EventManager.updateEvent (~line 520): if credentialFromDB is null or app?.slug is missing, updateEvent is called unguarded, throwing a TypeError and aborting processing of remaining calendar references; should be guarded like the create path

handleNewBooking.ts (~line 1080): evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is a no-op when destinationCalendar is null, silently dropping team destination calendars; also users.slice(1) may still include the organizer in dynamic-group bookings producing duplicate entries and duplicate events on the same calendar

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is explicitly set to `... ? [..] : ... ? [..] : null`, so it can be null. The later `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }` becomes a no-op when null, silently dropping collected team destination calendars (no fallback to initialize an array). Also, `teamMemberPromises = users.slice(1).map(...)` assumes the organizer is at `users[0]`, but for the dynamicUserList branch `prisma.user.findMany({ username: { in: dynamicUserList } })` does not guarantee ordering; thus the organizer may appear in `slice(1)`, causing their destinationCalendar to be added again and potentially leading to duplicate destinations and duplicate event creation (createAllCalendarEvents loops over destinationCalendar entries).

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestRescheduleHandler.ts (~line 237) drops the user.destinationCalendar fallback, so reschedule requests for bookings without a booking-level DC carry an empty destinationCalendar array and events may not be removed from the user's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In requestRescheduleHandler.ts the old code already had no user.destinationCalendar fallback: `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` (a redundant self-fallback). The diff changes this to an array form `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar] : []`, but it does not remove any `user.destinationCalendar` fallback because none existed in the shown code. The finding’s claim that a user-level fallback was dropped is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.updateEvent (~lines 515-525) pushes unawaited promises into result without await in both branches, causing unhandled rejections and mixing raw promises into the EventResult-typed array

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `result.push(updateEvent(...))` inside `EventManager.updateEvent` (both the `credentialId` and non-`credentialId` branches), which means `result` temporarily contains Promises. However, the diff snippet does not show what `result` is ultimately returned as (e.g., whether it is wrapped in `await Promise.all(result)`), so the claim that this causes “unhandled rejections” and that a Promise array is returned where `EventResult[]` is expected is not verifiable from the provided diff. Collecting promises into an array is also a common pattern when they are awaited later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organization slug behavior silently inverted in create.handler.ts (~line 148): !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug } → IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {} inverts which mode sets slug vs requestedSlug, so orgs created without team billing enabled get no slug at all, breaking org URL resolution

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts the spread condition for setting `slug` is flipped from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This means when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug` is set (since `requestedSlug` is also gated on `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). Previously, non-team-billing mode set `slug` directly. The diff therefore introduces a real behavior change where orgs created without team billing enabled may end up without any slug value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 DB queries and fully sequential event creation in createAllCalendarEvents: per-destination loop issues prisma.credential.findUnique and awaits createEvent serially, scaling latency linearly with host count; same shape duplicated in updateAllCalendarEvents (~lines 493-540)

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new per-destination loop does `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` inside the loop when a credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, and then does `await createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` before moving to the next destination. This makes both credential lookup and event creation effectively sequential and can produce N+1 DB queries and linearly increasing latency as `event.destinationCalendar` grows. A similar per-reference pattern (including per-item `prisma.credential.findUnique`) is introduced in the updated calendar-reference loop in `updateAllCalendarEvents` logic (the `calendarReference` is now a filtered array and is iterated). This is a concrete performance/architecture concern created by the diff, not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead fallback in Google updateEvent/deleteEvent (CalendarService.ts ~lines 253, 312): destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy so find compares against undefined and can never match, causing calendarId to be undefined and update/delete to fail after wasting OAuth token fetch and API round-trip

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar id as:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
(and similarly for `calendarId` in `deleteEvent`).

That `find(...)` branch is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`/"". This will not match any normal `externalId` values, making the fallback effectively dead and leaving `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` undefined, which can break update/delete requests (at minimum selecting the wrong calendar or relying on later unintended fallbacks). The finding is directly grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateEvent called without await inside credential loop (EventManager.ts ~line 540): promises collected into result but never awaited; if credential resolves to undefined, updateEvent(undefined, ...) rejections are only handled via outer catch which discards per-credential results

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `result.push(updateEvent(...))` inside a loop after `calendarReference` was changed to an array, but it does not show the end of the try block / return statement for this function. Without seeing whether the code later does `await Promise.all(result)` (or equivalent), the claim that the promises are "never awaited" cannot be verified from this diff. Likewise, the assertion about rejections being handled only via the outer catch depends on how the collected promises are ultimately awaited/returned, which is not present in the shown hunk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-credential event duplication on non-credentialId destinations: else branch creates an event on every credential of the integration type, so multiple destinations with the same integration fan out to all matching credentials, duplicating external API calls and calendar events

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new loop over `event.destinationCalendar` adds an `else` branch when a `destination` has no `credentialId`: it filters `this.calendarCredentials` by `c.type === destination.integration` and then creates an event for *each* matching credential (`Promise.all(... createEvent(c, event))`). Because this happens *inside the loop*, if `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple entries with the same `integration` and missing `credentialId`, the same set of credentials will be processed repeatedly, causing duplicated external API calls and duplicated calendar events. This behavior is directly visible in the diff around the `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking teamMemberPromises no longer short-circuits (~line 985): always maps users.slice(1) instead of conditional on users.length > 1, though impact is a no-op slice for single-user bookings

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `handleNewBooking` does change `teamMemberPromises` from a conditional (`users.length > 1 ? users.slice(1).map(...) : []`) to an unconditional `users.slice(1).map(...)`. However, `slice(1)` already returns an empty array when `users` has 0 or 1 elements, so the result is identical in those cases. This is not a defect or meaningful issue introduced by the diff—just a minor refactor with no behavioral impact for single-user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P0] Breaking change to public Calendar interface signature: createEvent(event, credentialId) now requires a second number argument without deprecation, breaking CalendarService.ts abstract base and other implementations not updated in the PR
[P0] TypeError crash when Google Meet location selected and destinationCalendar is null/empty: EventManager.ts destructures mainHostDestinationCalendar and accesses .integration unguarded

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then immediately evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and accessing `.integration` will throw a TypeError. The diff also introduces multiple call sites that can produce `destinationCalendar: []` (e.g. `bookingReminder.ts`, `webhook.ts`) or `null` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one), making this crash path real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1] Webhook payload shape drift: destinationCalendar changes from null/single object to array in externally-delivered CalendarEvent, breaking third-party consumers without versioning

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object/null to an array across the codebase (`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`, `packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts`). It also updates an end-to-end webhook test expectation from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []` (`apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`), and multiple event payload constructions now wrap a single destination calendar into an array or default to `[]` (e.g., `apps/web/pages/api/cron/bookingReminder.ts`, `packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts`). This is a real payload-shape drift that could break external webhook consumers, but the diff doesn’t prove it’s an unintended defect—more an API/compatibility/versioning concern created by the refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1] Google updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is dead code: find compares against undefined when externalCalendarId is falsy, losing previous destinationCalendar?.externalId fallback and sending calendarId: undefined

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new fallback logic for `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` is incorrect: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, it does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which compares `cal.externalId` to `undefined` and therefore will typically return `undefined` even if `destinationCalendar` contains entries. This removes the previous fallback behavior (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` when it was a single object) and can result in failing to pick a destination calendar ID when `externalCalendarId` is not provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1] createAllCalendarEvents DB-fallback credential bypasses calendarCredentials filtering and invalid state; credentialFromDB.app.slug as appName may mis-shape reference-type matching downstream

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, if a `destination.credentialId` isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the new logic fetches it directly from the DB (`prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })`) and then proceeds to call `createEvent` with that credential. This bypasses the prior in-memory filtering/selection logic (which implicitly constrained what credentials are used) and does not validate that the fetched credential belongs to the current user/team context, matches `destination.integration`, or is usable (e.g., `invalid === false`). The concern about `credentialFromDB.app.slug` shaping downstream matching is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff; the bypass/absence of validation is the concrete diff-grounded issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1] Recorded externalCalendarId reference may not match actual calendar event was created on (Google falls back to 'primary'), causing updateEvent/deleteEvent to target wrong calendarId and orphan events

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly tries to prevent the mismatch described: `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` now selects the calendar by matching `credentialId` against `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` (`find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`) and only falls back to `"primary"` when no matching destination calendar is found. In the main multi-destination path (`EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`), `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` is only used when `destination.credentialId` exists, which should make the `find(...credentialId...)` succeed and thus keep the created calendarId aligned with the recorded `externalId`. If the code does fall back to `primary` (no matching destination for that credential), the call site generally does not pass an `externalId` (so `result.externalId` would be `undefined`), meaning the specific claim of recording a non-primary externalCalendarId while creating on primary is not directly supported by what’s shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P2] Only organizer's destination calendar persisted on booking despite destinationCalendar accumulating all COLLECTIVE hosts; post-booking flows only see first host's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking`, for COLLECTIVE team events the code explicitly accumulates multiple destination calendars into `evt.destinationCalendar` (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), but when persisting the booking it only connects the first one: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (so only one destinationCalendar is saved on the Booking). Downstream flows shown in the diff build `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar`/`user.destinationCalendar` as a single-element array (or empty), so they will only ever see that first persisted calendar, not the full COLLECTIVE set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P2] handleCancelBooking recurring-deletion loop nested inside bookingCalendarReference loop, multiplying duplicate delete calls per reference per credential

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookingCalendarReference` was changed from a single `.find(...)` result to an array via `.filter(...)`, and the deletion logic is now wrapped in `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) { ... }`. Inside that outer loop, the recurring-event branch builds `promises` by iterating over *all* calendar credentials (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar"))`) and then iterates `updatedBookings` to delete events, pushing each delete into `apiDeletes`. Because this whole recurring deletion block is nested inside the per-reference loop, if there are multiple calendar references (which is now plausible given the multi-destination calendar refactor), the same set of deletes will be executed once per reference, multiplying duplicate delete calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P3] requestReschedule drops the user-level destinationCalendar fallback entirely, inconsistent with other handlers in the PR

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts`, the new logic sets `destinationCalendar` to `[bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar]` or `[]` (no fallback). Other updated handlers in this diff consistently fall back to the user-level destination calendar (e.g., `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `paypal-webhook.ts`, `webhook.ts`), so requestReschedule will produce an event with an empty `destinationCalendar` array when the booking has none, potentially breaking downstream calendar handling that expects a selected calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Crash on undefined destinationCalendar in EventManager: the Meet fallback destructures evt.destinationCalendar but accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, throwing TypeError when destinationCalendar is [] or element is undefined

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the Meet fallback now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without null/undefined guarding. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `undefined`, `null`, or `[]` (which several call sites in this diff now set, e.g. `destinationCalendar: []`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` will be `undefined` and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` will throw a `TypeError` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead fallback in Google CalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent: find() compares cal.externalId against falsy externalCalendarId, so the fallback can never match, leaving selectedCalendar/calendarId undefined instead of falling back to destinationCalendar.externalId

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` set `selectedCalendar/calendarId` like `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the branch where fallback is needed), the `find()` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will not match any real `externalId`, so the fallback returns `undefined` instead of using a destination calendar externalId (e.g., first/primary). This leaves the calendar id undefined and breaks the intended fallback behavior compared to the previous implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent fallback to "primary" calendar in Google createEvent when destinationCalendar credentialId doesn't match the used credential or lacks a credentialId, placing events in the wrong calendar with no error or warning

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target calendar is chosen only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and the API call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. This means if the destination calendar entry has no `credentialId` (or doesn’t match the passed `credentialId`), `selectedCalendar` is `undefined` and the event is silently inserted into the Google "primary" calendar with no error/warning. This matches the finding and can place events in an unintended calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team destination calendars silently dropped in handleNewBooking when evt.destinationCalendar is null for collective events, since optional chaining on push discards all team destination calendars; also teamDestinationCalendars populated via mutation inside .map() async callbacks (fragile)

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking, evt.destinationCalendar is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). For collective team events, team calendars are then appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If evt.destinationCalendar is null, optional chaining makes the push a no-op, so team members’ destination calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently dropped. This defect is visible directly in the diff. The additional note about mutating `teamDestinationCalendars` inside the async `.map()` callbacks is also grounded (shared mutable array in concurrent async callbacks), though the drop via `?.push` is the clearer correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateEventReferences in EventManager may call updateEvent with undefined credential when reference.credentialId is set but credential is deleted/missing, aborting the reference loop and leaving partially-updated multi-calendar bookings (missing if (!credential) continue guard)
matched_golden_ids: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same scenario: when reference.credentialId exists but the corresponding credential is missing/deleted, updateEvent is invoked with an undefined credential, potentially causing a runtime error. It also suggests adding a guard to handle the missing credential, aligning with the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-awaited updateEvent promises in EventManager loop at ~520-527 push raw promises, risking unhandled rejections that abort processing of remaining references

adjudication.rationale: In the shown EventManager changes, `result.push(updateEvent(...))` does push promises without `await`, but the diff does not show what happens to `result` afterward (e.g., `await Promise.all(result)`), so the claim of "non-awaited" promises and resulting unhandled rejections cannot be verified from the provided hunks. The finding asserts a specific failure mode (unhandled rejections aborting remaining processing) that is not demonstrated in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule handler drops the user destinationCalendar fallback (uses [] instead of booking.user.destinationCalendar), inconsistent with other handlers fixed in this PR

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts`, the pre-change code was `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` (no `bookingToReschedule.user.destinationCalendar` fallback at all). The new code wraps `bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar` in an array or uses `[]` when absent. So the finding's claim that this diff “drops the user destinationCalendar fallback” is not supported by the shown diff; there was no such fallback to drop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB-fetched credentials in EventManager and handleCancelBooking are used without checking invalid flag or that the app is a calendar integration, causing per-booking runtime failures instead of being skipped

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new code paths that fetch credentials from DB and immediately use them to call calendar operations without re-applying any filtering/validation that may exist on the in-memory `this.calendarCredentials`. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when a `destination.credentialId` isn’t found, it does `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` and constructs a `credential` object (including `invalid: credentialFromDB.invalid`) but never checks `invalid` before calling `createEvent(credential, ...)`. Similar DB-fetch-and-use happens in `EventManager.updateBookingReferences` and in `handleCancelBooking` (fetching `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId }})` and then `getCalendar(calendarCredential)`), again without checking `invalid` or otherwise confirming it’s a usable calendar credential. The claim about “per-booking runtime failures” isn’t directly provable from the diff alone (depends on `getCalendar` behavior), but the missing validation on DB-fetched credentials is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent/deleteEvent dead fallback: in else branch externalCalendarId is falsy so find() never matches, expression always undefined, silently regressing calendar targeting to 'primary'/'undefined'

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the target calendar as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, the `find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will almost always return no match, yielding `undefined`. This is a regression from the prior behavior that used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (when destinationCalendar was a single object) and will cause updates/deletes to fall back to an unintended default calendar (or pass undefined), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create.handler.ts:150 unrelated change inverts logic for slug — previously set when team billing disabled, now only when enabled — unrelated to PR purpose
matched_golden_ids: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: the conditional logic for setting `slug` was inverted (previously set when team billing was disabled, now only when enabled). While it doesn't mention the additional interaction with `requestedSlug` and the resulting both/neither states, it identifies the underlying logic inversion described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts: promise-builder map mutates outer teamDestinationCalendars array as side effect, fragile to refactoring

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, `teamMemberPromises = users.slice(1).map(async (user) => { ... teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar); ... await getTranslation(...) })` mutates the outer `teamDestinationCalendars` array as a side effect while building an async promise list, and later uses it via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. While the current code pushes before the first `await` (so it’s effectively synchronous today), the pattern is fragile and easy to break by refactoring (e.g., moving the `push` after an `await`), and it mixes data collection with async work unnecessarily.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts: isTeamEventType && schedulingType === 'COLLECTIVE' is redundant since isTeamEventType already includes COLLECTIVE

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, `isTeamEventType` is defined to be true for both `COLLECTIVE` and `ROUND_ROBIN` (it checks `['COLLECTIVE','ROUND_ROBIN'].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`). Later, the code intentionally further narrows behavior to only the `COLLECTIVE` case: `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === 'COLLECTIVE' && user.destinationCalendar) { ... }`. This is not redundant; it excludes `ROUND_ROBIN` while still requiring a team event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts: evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...) silently drops all team members' calendars when destinationCalendar is null for collective events

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [..] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [..] : null`. For collective team events, team member destination calendars are accumulated into `teamDestinationCalendars`, then appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If both `eventType.destinationCalendar` and `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` are missing, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so the optional-chained `push` is a no-op and all collected team member calendars are dropped with no fallback to `[]` or initialization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts: ~25-line credential-fetch + hand-mapping block duplicated in createAllCalendarEvents and update; extract getCredentialById helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds essentially the same “fetch credential from DB + hand-map into CredentialWithAppName” block in two places in EventManager.ts: (1) in createAllCalendarEvents(), when a destination.credentialId isn’t found in this.calendarCredentials it calls prisma.credential.findUnique(include app.slug) and then manually builds a credential object; (2) in update workflow (the loop over calendarReference), it repeats the same prisma.credential.findUnique(include app.slug) + manual mapping when reference.credentialId isn’t found. This is a maintainability/duplication issue introduced by the change, not a direct functional defect; extracting a shared getCredentialById helper would reduce divergence risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts: raw Prisma queries inside EventManager couple orchestration layer to persistence (layer leak)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds direct persistence access inside `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, e.g. in `createAllCalendarEvents` it does `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` to fetch credentials when not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, and similarly in the booking update flow it fetches credentials from DB when missing (`prisma.credential.findUnique({ ... where: { id: reference.credentialId } })`). This couples the EventManager orchestration layer to Prisma/persistence (a layer leak) introduced by the change, but it’s an architectural concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts: hand-rolled credential field mapping will silently break if Credential model changes

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, when a credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the code fetches it from Prisma and then manually constructs a `credential` object by enumerating fields (`appName`, `id`, `type`, `key`, `userId`, `teamId`, `invalid`, `appId`). This hand-rolled mapping is diff-grounded and creates maintenance risk: if the `Credential`/`CredentialWithAppName` shape changes (new required fields, renamed fields, etc.), this path may diverge from the canonical model unless kept in sync. This is a design/robustness concern rather than a directly verifiable functional bug in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts:418-485: same credential-fetch block duplicated a third time with a different shape (no app include, no mapping), so getCalendar receives inconsistent credential shapes across call sites

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts` the new fallback when a `credentialId` reference exists but the credential is not in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then passes that raw Prisma `Credential` object to `getCalendar` (no `app` include, no mapping to the `{ appName, ... }` shape used elsewhere). In this same diff, `EventManager` adds a similar “fetch credential from DB” path but includes `app.slug` and maps into a custom credential object. This creates duplicated logic with inconsistent credential shapes across call sites, which is a maintainability/consistency concern, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it breaks `getCalendar` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: destinationCalendar ternary normalization repeated ~8 times across handlers; extract a getBookingDestinationCalendars(booking, user) helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces repeated normalization of `destinationCalendar` from a single `DestinationCalendar | null` into a `DestinationCalendar[]` across multiple handlers using similar ternaries, e.g. `bookingReminder.ts` (`selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`), Stripe webhook (`packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts`), PayPal webhook, `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts`, `handleCancelBooking.ts`, etc. This is not a correctness defect, but it is a concrete maintainability issue created by the change: duplicated logic increases risk of inconsistent behavior (some return `null`, some `[]`) and future edits needing to touch many call sites. Extracting a shared helper like `getBookingDestinationCalendars(booking, user)` would reduce duplication and enforce consistent semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule.handler.ts:239: fallback omits user.destinationCalendar unlike all other handlers (pre-diff code was already buggy, ORing destinationCalendar with itself)

adjudication.rationale: In `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, the diff changes `destinationCalendar` to `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`, which still provides no fallback to `bookingToReschedule.user.destinationCalendar`. Other handlers in this diff consistently fallback to the user’s destination calendar when the booking’s is missing (e.g. `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts`). Given the previous code was effectively `A || A`, this change preserves the omission and now yields an empty array when `bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar` is null, likely breaking calendar behavior for reschedule requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Main host destination calendar destructuring duplicated 8+ times across CalendarService and Google/Lark/Office365 services; extract shared getMainHostDestinationCalendar(event) util

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same pattern added repeatedly to adapt to `destinationCalendar` becoming an array, e.g. `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` (or similar) in multiple places: GoogleCalendarService (createEvent/updateEvent), LarkCalendarService (createEvent/createAttendees/updateEvent/deleteEvent), Office365CalendarService (createEvent), BaseCalendarService (at least two locations), EventManager (location fallback), and BrokenIntegrationEmail. This is not a correctness defect by itself, but it is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue introduced by the change: the “main host destination calendar” selection logic is duplicated across services, increasing the risk of future inconsistencies. Extracting a shared helper (e.g., `getMainHostDestinationCalendar(event)`) would address this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarManager.ts:229: createEvent accepts externalId parameter but never uses it except echoing back, so externalCalendarId in references may claim a calendar the event wasn't actually created in (e.g. Google 'primary' fallback)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, `createEvent(credential, calEvent, externalId?)` passes only `(calEvent, credential.id)` into the calendar integration (`calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`) and never uses `externalId` to influence which calendar the event is created in, only echoing it back in the returned result (`externalId, credentialId`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, calendar selection is based on `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and if that lookup fails it falls back to `"primary"`. Meanwhile, `packages/core/EventManager.ts` records `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`. Therefore, if the integration falls back to `primary` (e.g., no matching destinationCalendar for that credential), references can store an `externalCalendarId` that does not correspond to the calendar actually used to create the event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar.d.ts: schedulingType leaked into CalendarEvent DTO coupling transport object to persistence enum; only consumer already has eventType in scope

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null;` to `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts` and imports `SchedulingType` from `@calcom/prisma/enums`, and `handleNewBooking.ts` sets `schedulingType: eventType.schedulingType` on the `CalendarEvent` object. This does couple the CalendarEvent DTO/type layer to a Prisma persistence enum (new cross-layer dependency). It’s an architectural/scope concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar.d.ts:221: interface requires createEvent(event, credentialId) but Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService implementations ignore credentialId — type-boundary mismatch; make it optional or update implementations

EventManager.ts:~117 — non-null-safe access to mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration crashes with TypeError when destinationCalendar is [] or null (e.g. Google-Meet events from confirm.handler, requestReschedule.handler, handleCancelBooking, bookingReminder, webhooks, or handleNewBooking with no destinationCalendar)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new array-based handling does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in the Meet fallback check. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `[]` or `null`/`undefined`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` will throw a `TypeError`. The diff also shows multiple paths now setting `destinationCalendar` to `[]` (e.g. `confirm.handler.ts`, `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, `bookingReminder.ts`, payment webhooks) or `null` (`handleNewBooking.ts`), making this crash scenario reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:~253 and ~312 — dead fallback in selectedCalendar: when externalCalendarId is falsy, find() can never match, resolving to undefined instead of destinationCalendar.externalId, causing Google API update with calendarId undefined or a no-op delete that orphans the event

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` (~244-253) and `deleteEvent` (~303-312) changed the falsy-`externalCalendarId` fallback from using `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (old single object) to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the exact condition that triggers the fallback), the `find()` predicate compares every `cal.externalId` to `undefined/null`, which will not match in normal cases, so the result is `undefined`. That can propagate into the Google API call as an undefined `calendarId` (or cause deletion to target the wrong/default calendar), potentially leaving the original event orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~555 — updateEvents merge path deletes only one old calendar reference on reschedule, leaving orphaned events for all other destination calendars on multi-destination bookings; find must become a filter/loop

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, `updateEvents` was updated to handle multiple calendar references by changing `calendarReference` from a single `find(...)` to `filter(...)` and looping over them. However, in the merge path (`if (newBookingId) { ... }`), it still does `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` (singular) and thus would delete only one old calendar event reference even if the booking has multiple `_calendar` references (which is now plausible with `destinationCalendar` being an array and multiple events being created). This can leave orphaned external events for the other references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~205 / CalendarManager.ts:~264 — createEvent returns externalId and credentialId unconditionally even when event creation failed (success=false, calError, or no calendar), so reference rows are written pointing to events that may not exist, masking real calendar write failures

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, `createEvent(...)` now always includes `externalId` (the passed-in calendar externalId) and `credentialId: credential.id` in the returned `EventResult` object (see the added fields in the return at the end), regardless of whether `creationResult` is `undefined` and/or `success` was set to `false` in the `.catch(...)`. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the mapped payloads now use `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId` for `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId` without checking `result.success`. However, the diff does not show the code that persists reference rows, so the claim that “reference rows are written pointing to events that may not exist” can’t be directly verified from this diff alone; it’s a plausible downstream concern based on the new data flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:~146 — silent fallback calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary" masks misrouted events; when no destinationCalendar matches the credentialId, the event is silently created on the user's primary calendar instead of erroring

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects `selectedCalendar` by matching `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, but still calls `calendar.events.insert` with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If no `destinationCalendar` entry matches the passed `credentialId`, the event is created on the Google "primary" calendar without signaling failure. This is compounded by `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` returning `externalId` from the caller (`createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`), so the system can record a non-primary `externalId` even though the event was actually inserted into `primary`, leading to inconsistent references and likely broken update/delete behavior later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:~119-125 — mainHostDestinationCalendar destructures destinationCalendar[0], so every host's event uses host #1's externalId as organizer email; wrong organizer email for non-first hosts may cause Google to reject or mangle attendee/organizer state

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `createEvent` now selects the target `calendarId` based on the passed `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`), but it sets the organizer attendee email from only the first destination calendar: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...; email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? ... : calEventRaw.organizer.email`. When `destinationCalendar` contains multiple entries (as introduced in this diff), events created for non-first credentials will still use destinationCalendar[0].externalId as the organizer email, which is inconsistent with the selected calendar/credential and can lead to incorrect organizer/attendee state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~500-530 — DB credential fetch failure calls updateEvent(undefined, ...), throwing and aborting updates for all remaining references in the loop (cascade failure), unlike createAllCalendarEvents which guards with if (credential)

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts within the new loop over `calendarReference` (around lines ~493-570), when `reference.credentialId` is present it sets `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0]` and, if falsy, attempts a DB fetch. However, after the DB fetch it unconditionally calls `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, ...))` without re-checking that `credential` is defined. If the credential is missing in memory and the DB lookup fails/returns null, `updateEvent` is invoked with `undefined`, which will throw and be caught by the outer try/catch—aborting updates for remaining references. This differs from `createAllCalendarEvents`, which explicitly guards with `if (credential)` before calling `createEvent`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:~990-1000 — team destination calendars built from users.slice(1) assumes users[0] is the organizer; if organizer isn't first, a host's destination calendar is silently dropped; also evt.destinationCalendar?.push silently discards all team destination calendars when destinationCalendar is null

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, `teamMemberPromises = users.slice(1).map(...)` and the comment “Organizer ... is not listed as a team member” implicitly assumes `users[0]` is the organizer. But `loadUsers()` can return users from `prisma.user.findMany({ where: { username: { in: dynamicUserList }}})` without any ordering, so the “first user” is not guaranteed to be the organizer; the first user’s `destinationCalendar` would be skipped from `teamDestinationCalendars` because only `users.slice(1)` are considered. Also, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is guarded by optional chaining, so team destination calendars are dropped entirely in that case instead of initializing the array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:~1875 — Prisma connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } depends on array element shape; a synthesized destination object without id would make Prisma throw at booking-time

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `evt.destinationCalendar` is populated from `eventType.destinationCalendar`, `organizerUser.destinationCalendar`, and `user.destinationCalendar` entries (and for COLLECTIVE, additional `user.destinationCalendar` values are pushed). These are Prisma `DestinationCalendar` objects, which include an `id`, and the code guards with `evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0` before doing `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`. The finding’s claim about a “synthesized destination object without id” is not supported by any code shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar.d.ts:~221 — interface mismatch: Calendar.createEvent now requires two args but Lark, Office365, and BaseCalendarService implementations still declare createEvent(event) and ignore credentialId, so credentialId-based selection only works for Google Calendar
matched_golden_ids: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same interface contract break: Calendar.createEvent now expects (event, credentialId), but implementations like Lark/Office365 (and BaseCalendarService) still only accept (event), meaning credentialId-based behavior won’t work consistently. This matches the golden issue, including noting it occurs in multiple places.
